title: Microsoft Teams: speaker attribution in BYOD rooms is on by default, with a PowerShell setting to turn it off
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing model, default state and governance controls match the Microsoft sources checked. It explicitly flags Microsoft's conflicting BYOD support wording and parameter example rather than presenting them as settled.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target date is July CY2025.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2025"

claims.claim: The roadmap record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Targeted Release.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Targeted Release"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and GCC.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Mac.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Mac"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new PowerShell setting named SpeakerAttributionBYOD in csTeamsAIPolicy for BYOD rooms.
claims.quote: New PowerShell setting (SpeakerAttributionBYOD in csTeamsAIPolicy), enabled by default, gives IT admins more control over speaker attribution in BYOD (bring your own device) meeting rooms.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: BYOD speaker attribution is enabled by default.
claims.quote: This setting can be set to Enabled or Disabled, and will be enabled by default.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the change enables clear speaker labels.
claims.quote: This enhances the experience for users by enabling clear speaker labels

claims.claim: The roadmap associates the change with richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The roadmap says users enrol profiles through Teams settings to be recognised.
claims.quote: Users just enroll profiles via Teams Settings to be recognized.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn makes BYOD-room speaker recognition available where the room host has Teams Premium or a Copilot licence.
claims.quote: BYOD Rooms: Intelligent Speakers available in rooms where the room host has either a Microsoft Teams Premium or Copilot license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: An add-on licensing model is supported by the qualifying Teams Premium licence.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams Premium is a Teams add-on license that allows organizations with Microsoft 365 subscriptions to enhance their Teams experience

claims.claim: The voice recognition page does not state whether other room-host licences qualify.
claims.quote: Searched: SpeakerAttributionBYOD pricing meter charge BYOD speaker recognition licensing Teams Enterprise. Read voice-recognition and the Teams Premium licensing comparison; the voice-recognition page names Teams Premium or Copilot for BYOD hosts, not other qualifying licences.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No Teams admin center control is documented for SpeakerAttributionBYOD.
claims.quote: Searched: "SpeakerAttributionBYOD" "admin center". Opened Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy, voice-recognition and voice-and-face-recognition; the latter says CsTeamsAIPolicy is accessible only through Microsoft PowerShell. Found no UI setting for BYOD attribution.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Disabled turns BYOD attribution off in the Global policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Disabled

claims.claim: SpeakerAttributionBYOD accepts Enabled to turn attribution on and Disabled to turn it off.
claims.quote: Setting to "Enabled" turns on speaker attribution in BYOD scenarios while "Disabled" will turn off the function.

claims.claim: The Identity parameter can target a custom Teams AI policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Test -SpeakerAttributionBYOD Disabled

claims.claim: A Teams admin center surface for assigning a custom Teams AI policy is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy" "admin center". Read Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice-and-face-recognition; assignment is documented through PowerShell and the enrollment article says the policy is accessible only through Microsoft PowerShell.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -PolicyName <policy name> -Identity <user> assigns a Teams AI policy to a user.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -PolicyName Test -Identity testuser@test.onmicrosoft.com
Assigns a given policy to a user.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy supports group assignment with Group and Rank.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy
    [[-PolicyName] <String>]
    [-Group] <String>
    -Rank <Int32>

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy supports tenant assignment with Global.
claims.quote:
Grant-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Global -PolicyName Test
Assigns a given policy to the tenant.

claims.claim: A Teams admin center switch for active voice enrolment is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "voice" "enrollment" "only through" "PowerShell". Read voice-and-face-recognition and Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy; policy configuration is PowerShell-only. The documented admin center experience views status and deletes data, rather than setting EnrollVoice.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled disables active voice enrolment in the Global policy.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity Global -EnrollVoice Disabled
Set Teams AI policy "EnrollVoice" value to "Disabled" for global as default.

claims.claim: EnrollVoice governs access to active voice enrolment.
claims.quote: EnrollVoice controls user access to active voice enrollment in the Teams app settings.

claims.claim: PassiveVoiceEnrollment independently governs express voice enrolment.
claims.quote: This is known as Express voice enrollment. This setting can also be individually set to Enabled or Disabled and operates independently of EnrollVoice.

claims.claim: Both EnrollVoice and PassiveVoiceEnrollment must be disabled to turn voice enrolment off completely.
claims.quote: As an organization, you have the option to Enable Active enrollment (via EnrollVoice) and/or Express enrollment (via PassiveVoiceEnrollment) for your users. To turn off voice enrollment completely, make sure to set both parameters to Disable.

claims.claim: The transcription setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows meeting transcription.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Meeting transcription requires the organiser's transcription policy to be enabled.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The user starting recording or transcription must also have transcription enabled.
claims.quote: The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Speaker identification requires transcription to be enabled.
claims.quote: Identification requires transcription to be enabled.

claims.claim: The BYOD room host is the person connecting their laptop to the Intelligent Speaker.
claims.quote: The room host is the person who connects their laptop to the Intelligent Speaker.

claims.claim: The BYOD requirements specify the Teams desktop client on Windows or macOS.
claims.quote:
BYOD Rooms:
Teams Desktop Client on Windows or macOS.

claims.claim: Learn says BYOD users need an updated Teams client.
claims.quote: Users need to make sure that their Teams client is updated.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users need an enrolled voice profile to be identified in a meeting space.
claims.quote: End users must have their voice profile enrolled to be identified in a meeting space.

claims.claim: Speaker recognition analyses vocal characteristics such as pitch, tone and speaking style to create a voiceprint.
claims.quote: Teams Rooms and BYOD Rooms use advanced technology called speaker recognition to analyze the distinct vocal characteristics of each speaker, such as pitch, tone, and speaking style, to create a voiceprint for each participant

claims.claim: Speaker recognition can show enrolled speakers by name in transcription.
claims.quote: Users who are enrolled are shown with their name in the transcription.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users must opt in to enrol even when recognition is available.
claims.quote: Even if the feature is available, users still need to opt in to enroll their voice and face and create their voice and face profile before they can start using voice and face recognition.

claims.claim: Each person gets a unique voice signature.
claims.quote: Each person gets a unique voice signature

claims.claim: Voice signatures are stored in the organisation's tenant in the Microsoft Cloud.
claims.quote: Each person gets a unique voice signature, stored securely in your organization's tenant in the Microsoft Cloud

claims.claim: A voice and face profile unused for one year is removed automatically.
claims.quote: In addition, a voice and face profile that isn't used for one year is removed automatically.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not use voice and face profiles to train models.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't use the voice and face profiles of users to train any models

claims.claim: Microsoft does not use profiles for purposes other than providing Teams voice and face recognition.
claims.quote: Microsoft doesn't use the voice and face profiles of users to train any models or for any other purposes other than providing the voice and face recognition feature in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Learn says Copilot needs a transcript attributed to every speaker to deliver summaries, insights and action items.
claims.quote: Copilot needs a meeting transcript, with attribution for every speaker, to deliver meeting summaries, insights, and action items.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users can unenrol after their organisation disables enrolment.
claims.quote: Users can delete their voice and face profile at any time using the Teams desktop app, even if their Enterprise administrator has turned off enrollment after they enrolled.

claims.claim: Learn says identification is supported only when the organiser's mailbox is in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: Identification features are supported only when the meeting organizer's mailbox is in Exchange Online. They aren't supported for on-premises Exchange or third-party calendars (for example, Google Calendar).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The voice recognition page also says BYOD scenarios are not supported for identification, alongside its hybrid-deployment qualification.
claims.quote: Hybrid deployments are supported only if Teams can access the organizer's calendar in the cloud. BYOD scenarios aren't supported for identification features.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The voice recognition page's example uses SpeakerAttributionForBYOD, unlike the cmdlet reference's SpeakerAttributionBYOD.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsAiPolicy -Identity Global -SpeakerAttributionForBYOD Enabled

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn says an assigned policy can take up to 48 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: After a policy is assigned, it can take up to 48 hours to take effect.

claims.claim: Learn says signing accounts out and back in makes the policy take effect sooner.
claims.quote: To get the policy to take effect sooner, accounts must be signed out and signed back in.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and price; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference and voice recognition page name no separate meter or charge for the setting.
claims.quote: Searched: SpeakerAttributionBYOD pricing meter charge BYOD speaker recognition licensing Teams Enterprise. Opened Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice-recognition in full; neither names a separate setting meter or charge.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and price
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference and voice recognition page do not publish Teams Premium or Copilot prices.
claims.quote: Searched: SpeakerAttributionBYOD pricing meter charge BYOD speaker recognition licensing Teams Enterprise. Read Set-CsTeamsAIPolicy and voice-recognition in full; they contain no Teams Premium or Copilot price.

claims.claim: Learn says BYOD users can connect any room speaker microphone to their laptops through USB.
claims.quote: Users can use any speaker microphone in a room and can connect it through USB to their laptops.

claims.claim: Learn says certified Intelligent Speaker hardware can provide higher recognition and transcription quality.
claims.quote: Certified intelligent speakers are designed with multiple microphones to provide high-quality audio, maximize accuracy in recognition and transcription

claims.claim: Learn recommends at most 10 in-person BYOD-room attendees for best transcript precision.
claims.quote: To ensure best precision for the transcript, we suggest limiting the number of in person attendees to a maximum of 10 people.

claims.claim: The documented BYOD limit for invitees with a voice profile is 50.
claims.quote: The current limitation for people invited with voice profile is currently 50.

claims.claim: Voice and face enrolments are available only up to GCC, not GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: No, voice and face enrollments are currently available only up to GCC and aren't available in GCCH or DOD environments.

claims.claim: The cited feature and policy pages do not name a specific administrator role for configuring the Teams AI policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams AI policy" "role"; Teams PowerShell administrator roles manage all policies Teams Administrator. Cited policy and enrollment pages name no specific role. The separate Entra roles reference gives Teams Administrator general Teams PowerShell rights.

claims.claim: New-CsTeamsAIPolicy creates a custom Teams AI policy.
claims.quote:
Enterprise administrators can create and assign a custom meeting policy to the users:
New-CsTeamsAIPolicy -Identity DisableEnrollment -EnrollVoice Disabled -EnrollFace Disabled

claims.claim: Teams admin center lets administrators view end-user voice and face enrolment status.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can now use Teams admin center to view end-user voice and face enrollment status and manage enrolled data directly from the admin experience.

claims.claim: Administrators can delete end-user voice and face profiles and enrolment data in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Enterprise administrators can also delete end-user voice and face profiles and enrollment data directly from the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot export end-user voice or face enrolment data through the admin experience.
claims.quote: Admins don't have access to export voice and face data, giving users full control over their face and voice data and profiles.

claims.claim: The voice-enrolment controls are separate from the control that turns BYOD speaker attribution off.
claims.quote: This cmdlet sets the EnrollFace, EnrollVoice, PassiveVoiceEnrollment, and SpeakerAttributionBYOD values within the csTeamsAIPolicy. These policies can be assigned to users, and each setting can be configured as "Enabled" or "Disabled".

claims.claim: The roadmap describes speaker labelling and Copilot insights, not an agent or an automated action.
claims.quote: This enhances the experience for users by enabling clear speaker labels and richer in-meeting and post-meeting insights with Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users just enroll profiles via Teams Settings to be recognized.

claims.claim: A medium cost rating reflects the documented qualifying add-on licence for room hosts.
claims.quote: Room hosts should have either Teams Premium or Copilot license. The room host is the person who connects their laptop to the Intelligent Speaker.
